POC / technical takeaways:
- Workload: multi-turn chat with embeddings for context + occasional re-ranking of search hits.
- Throughput target: sustained 120 reqs/sec peak, 30k embeddings/day.
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for chat generation at 512 token context. Met on Dedicated.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-level — wants predictable monthly commit; overage must be bounded.
- Model preference: prefer open-model variants (gpt-like open checkpoint). Will accept Redwood-verified quantized models if quality delta <1% on their eval set.
- Ops notes: KV prefix caching reduced token throughput cost ~22% in POC. Int8 quantization acceptable for most prompts; flagged two templates where hallucination increased slightly.

Pricing / packaging negotiation (current position):
- Redwood proposal (initial): 12-month Dedicated commit = 150M tokens/month equivalent; monthly fee $12,500; burst pool 2x baseline at 1.5x unit price; overage billed at 150% of committed unit price; ramp schedule: Q1 at 50% commit, Q2 75%, Q3+ 100%.
- Quantile counter: wants 9-12 month term with blended ARR target $75k-$125k, lower overage cap (no more than 125%), and guaranteed 30% burst at committed price for first 6 months. Also requests a clause to increase commit mid-term without penalty and an initial 60-day billing grace while they ramp usage.
- Key negotiation items to resolve: commit baseline, overage multiplier cap, burst capacity pricing and guaranteed burst minimum, ramp schedule enforcement, early-exit / step-down terms for underutilization.

- Quantile needs SSO (SAML) + SOC2 type II evidence.
- Data residency: customer data must be stored in US-only tenants; Redwood to provide audit logging retention 2 years.
- KMS: they use AWS KMS; require timeline for KMS integration into Dedicated control plane.

- Legal pushing on overage cap and exit terms (wants soft cap and ability to renegotiate at 6 months).
- Security team requires SOC2 and KMS commitment before CISO sign-off.
